assessment.nobel_worthiness: Moiré flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which correlated insulators, superconductivity and magnetism are tunable in one device. From an electronic-structure perspective it is a rare case where a continuum-model prediction of a flat band at a magic angle was followed by a decisive experiment, and where the physics of correlated electrons with controllable bandwidth is now widely reproduced and extended to many moiré systems.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the 2011 continuum-model prediction of the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 observation of correlated insulating states and superconductivity. Theory and experiment are clearly separable, so a three-way split is defensible; other contributors (for example the earlier twisted-graphene theory and the Cao/Fatemi/Jarillo-Herrero team members) are not in the supplied names and the credit boundary is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Core observations have been reproduced by many groups over about seven years and the platform has produced further discoveries. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are still debated, but the discovery of the flat-band correlated regime is stable; recognition is timely though arguably early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and some correlated phases remain unresolved.
Sample inhomogeneity (twist-angle disorder) complicates reproducibility of detailed phase diagrams.
Credit may extend beyond the supplied names, which I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall state and topological insulators reshaped how band structure is classified, linking spin-orbit coupling to protected edge and surface states. It is conceptually original, rigorous and has had lasting impact across materials, spintronics and quantum-device ideas; band-structure calculations were central to identifying real materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall proposal in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe/CdTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan's surface-state ARPES work on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 is a separate experimental strand, and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Zhang are not credited here, so the three-name configuration leaves unresolved who else has equal claim.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in several materials and by multiple techniques for over fifteen years; the interpretation is stable. The risk is not maturity but the contested credit among theorists and experimentalists; the recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Hasan, who are not all in the supplied names.
The candidate B025 covers an overlapping discovery and ballots could split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and later coherent-tunnelling MgO junctions, underpin read heads and magnetic random-access memory. This is a direct application of spin-dependent electronic structure, in a field I know well: spin polarization of the tunnelling current and band-symmetry filtering were understood through first-principles theory. The impact on technology is large and well documented.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin (and Yuasa, who is not credited here) achieved the giant MgO-based TMR in 2004. The theory of symmetry filtering (Butler, Mathon) is outside the supplied names. Since the 2007 prize recognized GMR, the committee would have to justify the separate step carefully.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely commercialised and thoroughly confirmed. Recognition timing is late rather than premature, with the main constraint being overlap with the 2007 GMR prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the GMR prize and uncertainty about whether TMR is a sufficiently distinct discovery.
Essential contributors to MgO TMR (Yuasa, Djayaprawira, Butler) are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED established strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators, providing the basis for readout, control and entanglement in superconducting quantum processors. It is a clear, original and demonstrably consequential idea, though it follows the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which makes the committee sensitive to adjacent recognition.
assessment.attribution: Blais et al. proposed the architecture in 2004, and Wallraff et al. demonstrated strong coupling in the same year with Schoelkopf's group; the three names are a natural configuration. Whether the prior 2025 award reduces the need for a further circuit-based prize is a judgement outside the technical credit question.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent replication in many laboratories and a still-growing technology. The interpretation is stable and well established.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize may argue for waiting.
Contributions from other superconducting-qubit groups to the dispersive readout are not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory made strongly correlated electrons tractable by mapping a lattice problem to a self-consistent impurity problem, and with LDA+DMFT it connects first-principles electronic structure with Mott physics. I know the method well and regard it as a conceptual advance with real quantitative applications. Whether it is a single decisive discovery or a long methodology programme is a fair question.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimensional limit, and Georges and Kotliar's impurity mapping, were the decisive steps; Metzner is not in the supplied names, and Vollhardt may reasonably be credited with the limit. The three supplied names are a plausible but incomplete configuration, and theory prizes of this kind face the difficulty of attributing a method-development community.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted over thirty years and systematically benchmarked, though accuracy for real materials remains tool-dependent. Not premature, but the Nobel tradition prefers a concrete discovery over a method.
uncertainties: Method development rather than a discovery about nature.
Missing credited contributors such as Metzner and Müller-Hartmann.
Quantitative reliability depends on solver and double-counting choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The impact on metrology is concrete, measurable and clearly lasting, and the result is outside my own field but evidently of the highest technical quality.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group developed the strontium clock to record accuracy and the quantum-many-body clock; two names give a clean allocation, although other groups (Lemonde, Gill, Hinkley/Ludlow) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks in several laboratories agree at the 1e-18 level, and the redefinition of the second is being considered. Timing is good.
uncertainties: The 2005 prize on frequency combs and 2012 prize on ion control already partly cover the area.
I am not a specialist in metrology and cannot independently verify the allocation of credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, giving direct access to Mott insulators, antiferromagnetic correlations and quantum dynamics. For a theorist of correlated electrons this is attractive as a quantum simulation of models I work with, though its impact on materials understanding is still partly prospective.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch-Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-Mott transition, and Esslinger realised the Fermi-Hubbard Mott insulator. With five credited names, any selection of three is a compromise; Cirac and Greiner have strong claims, and Jaksch is absent.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely, and the field has delivered quantum-gas microscopy and observation of magnetic order. The remaining open question is whether simulations will resolve open problems such as d-wave pairing.
uncertainties: Five credited names exceed three laureate seats.
Open question whether the simulation has yet answered unsolved problems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of iron-pnictide superconductivity opened a second high-temperature family with multiband character, and electronic-structure calculations have been central to the discussion of nesting, magnetism and pairing symmetry. The discovery is clear, but its impact on a unifying mechanism is limited.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono reported superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx in 2008; the discovery is cleanly attributed, though Hosono's earlier work and the quick follow-up by Chinese groups raising Tc are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups and now stable, but the pairing mechanism remains debated and no application has emerged, so the Nobel case is moderate.
uncertainties: Subsequent Tc enhancements by other groups are outside the supplied credit.
